  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 6, 2022  2
   Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. 2022 CONFLICT-OF-INTEREST CODE BIENNIAL UPDATE

  Under the Political Reform Act, public agencies are required to adopt a conflict-
  of-interest code designating positions required to file Statements of Economic
  Interests (Form 700) and assigning disclosure categories specifying the types of
  interests to be reported. The conflict-of-interest code must be reviewed every
  two years so that amendments may be made as needed. There is no fiscal
  impact.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council effectuate the necessary changes to the
  City’s Conflict of Interest Code by adopting Resolution No. 22-56 entitled, “A
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel, California, amending
  the City of San Gabriel Conflict of Interest Code and rescinding Resolution No.
  20-43.”

  D. ORDINANCE NO. 684 ADOPTING POLICE DEPARTMENT LEXIPOL POLICY,
  SECTION 707, MILITARY EQUIPMENT, PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL (AB)
  481 MILITARY EQUIPMENT ACQUISITION, USE, AND REPORTING – 2ND
  READING & ADOPTION

  Ordinance No. 684 was approved at introduction by a 5-0 vote of the City
  Council at the August 16, 2022, City Council regular meeting. There is no fiscal
  impact directly related to the adoption of this policy.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  684 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of San Gabriel, California,
  adopting Police Department Lexipol Policy, Section 707, Military Equipment,
  pursuant to Assembly Bill (AB) 481 Military Equipment Acquisition, Use, and
  Reporting.”

  E. COMMISSIONER REMOVAL FOR NON-ATTENDANCE

  The City’s Rules of Order for City Meetings provide for declaring a commission
  seat vacant after a specified number of unexcused absences. The City Council

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 6, 2022  3
   is requested to make this declaration for a Community Services Commission
  seat.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council declare the Community Services
  Commission seat currently held by Bronwyn Velazquez vacant, effective
  immediately, and direct staff to advertise the position and begin accepting
  applications.

  F. COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION PROPOSED SCOPE, PURPOSE AND
  2022 ANNUAL WORKPLAN

  To help guide the commissioners’ work for the year and beyond and falling in
  alignment with the recommendation from the Human Equity, Access and
  Relations (HEAR) Commission, the Commission has developed a scope, purpose
  and annual workplan. The Commissioners have had open and constructive
  dialogue to develop an enduring scope and purpose that best fits in alignment
  with the intent of the CS Commission as well as the City of San Gabriel’s mission
  statement.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and approve the Community
  Services Commission’s Scope, Purpose and 2022 Annual Workplan, as
  presented above.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. INCLUSIONARY HOUSING AND DENSITY BONUS

  In recent years, both the community and City Council have expressed interest
  in the introduction of an Inclusionary Housing Ordinance and updating the
  City’s existing Density Bonus Ordinance. This report provides information on
  inclusionary housing and density bonus and implementation of Programs 14
  and 16 in the 2021-2029 Housing Element. There is no fiscal impact with the
  adoption of the Legislative Platform.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 6, 2022  4
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and discuss the
  Recommendation Memorandum, provide direction to staff on the development
  of an Inclusionary Housing Ordinance and updating the City’s existing Density
  Bonus Ordinance, and provide steps on the adoption of both ordinances at a
  future City Council meeting.

  B. AMENDMENT TO THE CITY’S FEE SCHEDULE TO INCLUDE PRICES AND
  FEES FOR THE DUMPLING AND BEER FESTIVAL

  For the past six years, the City has held its signature Dumpling and Beer Festival.
  This outdoor community festival celebrates the region’s diverse cultures
  through popular food and drink. The event is free and open to the public,
  through purchased tickets are required for guests 21 years of age or older to
  enter the beer garden area. In addition to an admission charge for the beer
  garden, the City also collects a vendor participation fee of $100 for a food truck,
  or $200 for a food booth. Historically, these fees were charged by a consultant
  hired by the City to run the event. The event is now run by the City directly and
  these fees continue to be implemented. Inclusion of the fees in the City’s Fee
  Schedule will have a positive impact on the General Fund.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council amend the City’s adopted Fee Schedule
  to include the vendor participation fee and charge of admission for the
  Dumpling and Beer Festival at the amounts recommended.

 8. PUBLIC COMMENT

 9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

 11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

 12. ADJOURNMENT

MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 6, 2022

I  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Ding called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:33
  P.M. on Tuesday, September 6, 2022, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South
  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vice Mayor Harrington.

  ROLL CALL
  Council Members Present:  Denise Menchaca, Carina Rivera, John Wu, Vice Mayor
  John R. Harrington, and Mayor Tony Ding .
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,

I  Police Chief Eugene Harris, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark,
  Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg de Vinck, Fire
  Chief  Steven  Wallace,  Human  Resources/Risk
  Management Director Edward Macias, Finance Director
  William Kaholokula, Community Development Director
  Aldo Cervantes, and Assistant City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Special City Council Meeting of September 6, 2022:

  A. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR (GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6)

  City Negotiators - City Manager Lazzaretto, City Attorney Lemieux, and Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Macias, Labor Relations Counsel Steve Filarsky.

  Regarding the following Employee Organizations - San Gabriel Police Officers'
  Association, San Gabriel Police Management Group, San Gabriel Firefighters'
  Association, San Gabriel Fire Management Group and all Unrepresented Employees.

I  City Attorney Lemieux announced that no reportable action was taken.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  how to request meeting agendas.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 5  September 6, 2022
   Hearing no objection, Mayor Ding stated the agenda order was approved.

  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. HISPANIC HERITAGE MONTH

  Mayor Ding made the presentation and Council Members Menchaca and Rivera
  commented on a book donation they made through the San Gabriel Educational

I  Foundation in honor of Hispanic Heritage Month.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Grace Yang, San Gabriel Library Manager, invited the community to provide input on
  the Library's services and detailed the methods available to do so.

  Debbie Kilgore, resident, commented on a recent issue with the San Gabriel Valley
  Humane Society and made a suggestion that one of the Council Members with a
  Hispanic background read the proclamation for Hispanic Heritage Month in the future.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member Wu,
  to approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4F as presented .

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  MENCHACA, RIVERA, WU, HARRINGTON, DING

I  NOES:
  ABSTAIN:
  ABSENT:
  NONE
  NONE
  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the following:

  1.  Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of August 2, 2022.
  2.  Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of August 5, 2022.
  3.  Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of August 6, 2022.
  4.  Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of August 16, 2022.
  5.  Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of August 16, 2022.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved August 5, 2022, August 12, 2022, and August 18, 2022,
  Registers of Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

I  c. 2022 CONFLICT-OF-INTEREST CODE BIENNIAL UPDATE
  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 22-56 entitled, "A Resolution of the City
  Council of the City of San Gabriel, California, amending the City of San Gabriel
  Conflict of Interest Code and rescinding Resolution No. 20-43."

  D. ORDINANCE NO. 684 ADOPTING POLICE DEPARTMENT LEXIPOL POLICY,
  SECTION 707, MILITARY EQUIPMENT, PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL (AB)
  481 MILITARY EQUIPMENT ACQUISITION, USE, AND REPORTING - 2ND
  READING & ADOPTION

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 5  September 6, 2022
   The City Council waived reading and adopted Ordinance No. 684 entitled, "An
  Ordinance of the City Council of San Gabriel, California, adopting Police
  Department Lexipol Policy, Section 707, Military Equipment, pursuant to Assembly
  Bill (AB) 481 Military Equipment Acquisition, Use, and Reporting ."

  E. COMMISSIONER REMOVAL FOR NON-ATTENDANCE

I  The City Council declared the Community Services Commission seat currently held
  by Bronwyn Velazquez vacant pursuant to the City's Rules of Order for City
  Meetings due to several unexcused absences, effective immediately, and directed
  staff to advertise the position and begin accepting applications.

  F. COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION PROPOSED SCOPE, PURPOSE AND
  2022 ANNUAL WORKPLAN

  The City Council approved the Community Services Commission 's Scope, Purpose
  and 2022 Annual Workplan, as presented.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING - None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS - None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. INCLUSIONARV HOUSING AND DENSITY BONUS

I  Planning Manager Samantha Tewasart and David Bergman of Lisa Wise Consulting,
  Inc. (LCW) made the presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included details of covenant restrictions and effects on
  property tax and homeowner association (HOA) fees for sellers and buyers of
  affordable -housing units; request for a comparison of Floor Area Ratio (FAR) under
  current and proposed standards; the inclusionary requirement would be citywide,
  but development is more likely in areas that allow higher density; the complexity
  of the information in the staff report and desire for future reports to be more easily
  understandable; nearby cities that have been successful with an inclusionary
  program; definition of and income basis for affordable housing; desire to include
  rental units; and including income provisions in the ordinance.

  Chasity Jennings-Nunez provided comments requesting the adoption of an
  lnclusionary Housing Ordinance as soon as possible and suggested that the
  Ordinance provide that 20% of units be rented or sold to very-low- and low-
  income households.

I  Debbie Kilgore, resident, stated that most residents don't understand the language
  in the presentation and requested meetings for the community that explain more
  simply; expressed concern about a shortage of parking spaces; and commented on
  high rental prices in the City.

  Isela Bowles, resident, commented on median household income in San Gabriel;
  cautioned about potential impacts of proposed changes on the City; and thanked
  Council Member Wu for his clarifying questions.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 5  September 6, 2022
   Discussion included that City Council direction is being sought on what the
  affordability level and percentage of affordable units should be before it goes to
  the Planning Commission for consideration; adoption of an inclusionary housing
  ordinance would not change development standards in the City; the need to show
  an economic study that development would still be feasible under new standards;
  City Council desire for the Planning Commission to be part of the discussion;
  Housing Needs Assessment statistics for the City; San Gabriel is a majority-rental
  City so it doesn 't make sense to exclude rentals; clarification of both income and
  housing-price in various income categories; a proposal for 15% for both for-sale

I  and rental properties; defaulting to the state for density-bonus standards; a
  request for more and simpler information; a suggestion for Council Members to
  let the City Manager know what information is desired in the next presentation;
  rental-property types; revisiting percentage numbers for the inclusionary
  ordinance every two years; having different percentage numbers for for-sale and
  rental units; assigning units to a certain income level doesn't guarantee buyers can
  qualify; and writing letters to legislators about providing special financing for low-
  income buyers.

  B. AMENDMENT TO TH E CITY'S FEE SCHEDULE TO INCLUDE PRICES AND FEES
  FOR THE DUMPLING AND BEER FESTIVAL

  Economic Development Director Caroline Velarde made the presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included a discount for early ticket sales and the allotment of
  800 tickets for the beer garden .

  There was no public comment.

I  Discussion included the ticket-sales timeline.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Harrington, seconded by Mayor Ding, to amend
  the City's adopted Fee Schedule to include the vendor participation fee and charge
  of admission for the Dumpling and Beer Festival at the amounts recommended,
  with the addition of a discount of $5 for ticket purchases up to two weeks prior to
  the event.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  MENCHACA, RIVERA, WU, HARRINGTON, DING
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN :  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Dr. Chasity Jennings-Nunez, Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR Chair),

I
  provided comments inviting the community to the first Mental Wellness Expo on
  September 18, 2022, from 12:00-4:00 P.M. in the Grapevine Arbor and Mission
  Playhouse Plaza, and thanked those who made the event possible.

  9. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto informed the City Council that he would not be present at
  the next regular City Council meeting as he will be out of town at a conference, and
  that Police Chief Harris will be sitting in for him at the meeting.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 5  September 6, 2022
   10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Council Member Rivera reported that she and Mayor Ding spent on a day with the San
  Gabriel Fire Department, commented on the experience, and thanked and
  commended Fire Department staff.

  Council Member Menchaca invited all to the Mental Wellness Expo, commented on a
  Pasadena Star News article on pickle ball that highlighted San Gabriel; and requested
  Fire Chief Wallace to speak about an upcoming 9/11 event.

I  Fire Chief Wallace announced the 21 st 9/11 Remembrance event on September 11 ,
  2022, at 6:30 A.M. at Fire Station 51.

  Council Member Wu reported on a September 1, 2022, Focus Plaza tenants' meeting,
  and expressed concern about landlord-tenant communication and his desire for the
  City to assist the business owners.

  Vice Mayor Harrington announced the Stunts and Fun event on September 11 , 2022,
  from 10:00 A.M. - 5:00 P.M. on Commercial Avenue just east of San Gabriel Boulevard
  and invited the community to attend after the 9/11 event.

  Mayor Ding echoed Council Member Rivera 's comments about the Fire Department
  visit and commented on his experience; expressed his desire for the City to facilitate
  communication between the Focus Plaza landlord and tenants; commented on a
  donation of Moon Cakes for the City's seniors sponsored by the Chinese-American
  Women 's Association; announced a school-supplies backpack giveaway on September
  8, 2022, for those who had pre-registered, sponsored by Los Angeles County, Kiwanis
  Club, and San Gabriel Hope Lions Club; reminded of the Stunts and Fun event

I  previously announced; and wished all a happy Moon Festival on September 10.

  11. CLOSED SESSION - None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 8:44 P.M

  Respectfully submitted:

  Approved this 20th day of September, 2022:

I  ~
  TONY DI NG, Mayor

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 5 of 5  September 6, 2022
